caption: The drawing depicts a wooden bench or pew with a high back and sides, characterized by rectangular panels on the armrests and sides. The top section features a semi-circular, fan-like decorative panel, adorned with painted patterns consisting of fan-shaped designs in red, blue, and green, arranged in a radiating fashion, and surrounded by a scalloped edge formed by rounded shapes. The fan motif extends upwards and is topped by a cross also decorated with bands of blue, red, and green color. The front arch above the seat is painted in a cream color, displaying symmetrical motifs in red, blue, and green, including geometric and floral elements. The side panels of the bench, as well as the lower front, are rendered in a natural wood tone with visible wood grain and slight shading to create a three-dimensional effect. The bench seat area is shaded darker, and each side panel includes a circular pierced pattern, possibly for ventilation. The overall composition is detailed and uses a palette primarily consisting of natural browns, creams, and primary colors for the decorative elements.
title: Confessional
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
